title: Organizational Governance Systems
coreMove: Teams protect value when their governance system maps authority to risk: local calls stay local, sponsor calls are explicit, and portfolio escalation happens early.

exampleSpecs.domain: a clinic scheduling replacement with a funding gap and a sponsor away at an offsite
exampleSpecs.audience: project managers who need authority before a risky change hardens
exampleSpecs.stakes: patients may wait longer if the rollout pauses, but unauthorized scope change can break the portfolio promise
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: two poor choices expose why decision rights and escalation must be visible before scope, funding, risk, or benefits shift

exampleSpecs.domain: a PMO review room where a project sponsor wants the team to decide a benefit tradeoff
exampleSpecs.audience: sponsors and PMO analysts clarifying authority before a steering meeting
exampleSpecs.stakes: a local choice could change a benefit forecast that the portfolio office already promised
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the exchange itself distinguishes local decision rights from sponsor and portfolio escalation

exampleSpecs.domain: a rail control software patch that looks smaller than an office refresh
exampleSpecs.audience: technical leads balancing speed with regulated safety exposure
exampleSpecs.stakes: a cheap change may deserve heavier oversight than a larger but low-risk effort
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the expected light review is overturned when safety-critical regulation and strategic importance surface

exampleSpecs.domain: a mobile product update where adoption metrics changed after a schedule slip
exampleSpecs.audience: product owners and portfolio coordinators handling fast, informal escalations
exampleSpecs.stakes: a team may keep moving locally after a benefit assumption has shifted
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a compressed chat shows when decision rights leave the team and move to sponsor and portfolio escalation

exampleSpecs.domain: a compliance intake desk that sorts change requests by default templates
exampleSpecs.audience: governance leads who need to stop a routine when risk signals appear
exampleSpecs.stakes: a routine low-review stamp could miss a regulated safety exposure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: an ordinary intake routine is interrupted, paused, and restarted around risk-based governance intensity

exampleSpecs.domain: a portfolio coordinator's desk on the morning of a review
exampleSpecs.audience: readers learning to see governance intensity in ordinary artifacts
exampleSpecs.stakes: two projects look similar in paperwork but different in exposure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a close observed desk scene shows governance rigor as a match to risk, not a one-size ritual
